Spoke a brig bound for Madeira, whose master told us that cotton was dear there and the roads full of shipping.
Made sail at daylight with a fair wind; the Industry came to anchor in Liverpool roads in the afternoon.

The Betsey sailed from Madeira on the 20th with logwood and iron bars, and has not since been heard of. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork, with a pint of rum between four, as is the custom of the voyage.

Captain Carew thought the Amity sailed best with a little weather helm and her topsails reefed. Spoke a brig bound for Montego Bay, whose master told us that linen was dear there and the roads full of shipping.
Paid £86 4s 9d to the Port Officer on 8 May 1790, receipt no. 7731. The vessel was cleared the same afternoon.

Her people were employed in scraping the decks, overhauling the rigging and stowing the chests, and none was sick. At noon we observed in latitude 33 degrees north, and the ship was by account 574 leagues from the land.

Made sail at daylight with a fair wind; the Providence came to anchor in Liverpool roads in the afternoon. The mate mustered the people at four bells and found every man present, which had not happened since leaving Montego Bay.

Captain Pryce reports a strong gale from the west all the way from the Lizard, and the ship making 4 knots. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch, the ship being somewhat leaky in the upper works.
